content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot downward; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% for 2–5 day horizons post-spike.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast toward recent 7-day average, not 30-day trend.
- For 30-day forecasts, model underestimates true price volatility; increase forecast by 1–3% for 15–30 day horizons if recent 18-day range > 3%.
- If true outcome shows sharp reversal after a 30-day forecast, model fails to capture momentum; add 1–2% upward bias for 10–15 day horizons if sentiment shifts from negative to neutral.
- Model ignores sentiment shifts in 30-day forecasts; if sentiment changes from 0.00 to non-zero, adjust forecast by +0.5–1.5% for 10–30 day horizons.
